q: Change to passive: "The officer signed the document."
options: The document was signed by the officer.
The document is signed by the officer yesterday.
The officer was signed by the document.
expl: Simple past passive is was/were + past participle.

q: Passive of "They are building a bridge" is:
options: A bridge is being built by them.
A bridge was built by them.
A bridge has been built by them.
expl: Present continuous passive is am/is/are being + past participle.

q: Passive of "She has completed the task" is:
options: The task has been completed by her.
The task was completed by her.
The task is completing by her.
expl: Present perfect passive is has/have been + past participle.

q: Active form of "The gate was opened by the guard" is:
options: The guard was opening by the gate.
expl: The doer becomes the subject and simple past is retained.

q: Passive of "They will announce the result tomorrow" is:
options: The result will be announced tomorrow.
expl: Future passive is will be + past participle.

q: Which sentence cannot normally be changed into passive voice?
expl: Intransitive "slept" has no object to become the passive subject.

q: Passive of "Open the door" is best expressed as:
options: Let open the door by you.
expl: Imperative passive can use "Let + object + be + past participle".

q: Passive of "Someone has stolen my bag" is:
expl: The unknown agent can be omitted in passive voice.

q: Passive of "The teacher is checking the papers" is:
options: The papers are being checked by the teacher.
expl: Present continuous passive requires "are being checked".

q: Passive of "You must obey the rules" is:
options: The rules have to obey you.
expl: Modal passive is modal + be + past participle.

q: Active of "English is spoken in many countries" is:
options: People speak English in many countries.
People spoke English in many countries only.
Many countries are speaking English people.
expl: An indefinite agent such as "people" is natural in active voice.

q: Passive of "They had finished the work" is:
expl: Past perfect passive is had been + past participle.

q: Passive of "Who wrote this letter?" is:
options: By whom was this letter written?
This letter was wrote by whom?
expl: Formal passive interrogative: "By whom was ... written?"

q: Which is a correct passive sentence?
expl: Present continuous passive uses "is being repaired".

q: Passive of "The storm damaged several houses" is:
options: Several houses were damaged by the storm.
Several houses are damage by storm.
The storm was damaged by several houses.
expl: Simple past passive uses were + past participle.

q: Passive of "They make cars here" is:
expl: Simple present passive is am/is/are + past participle.

q: Passive of "The committee may approve the plan" is:
options: The plan may be approved by the committee.
expl: Modal passive uses may + be + past participle.

q: Active of "The message was sent by Ali" is:
options: Ali sends the message now necessarily.
Ali was sent the message by it.
expl: The passive subject becomes the object and the agent becomes subject.

q: Passive of "They were watching the match" is:
options: The match was being watched by them.
expl: Past continuous passive is was/were being + past participle.

q: In passive voice, the main verb is normally in the:
expl: Passive constructions require a form of be plus the past participle.

q: Change to indirect speech: He said, "I am tired."
options: He said that I am tired.
He said that he was tired.
He says that he was tired.
He said that he is tired yesterday.

q: She said, "I have finished my work."
options: She said that she had finished her work.
She said that she has finished my work.
She said she finished her work tomorrow.
She told that she had finish work.
expl: Present perfect normally backshifts to past perfect.

q: He said to me, "You are late."
options: He said me that I was late.
He told me that I was late.
He told that you were late.
He said to I that I was late.
expl: "Said to" commonly becomes "told + object"; "you" becomes "I" by context.

options: Ali said that he would come the next day.
Ali said that I will come tomorrow.
Ali says that he would come yesterday.
Ali told he would came next day.
expl: "Will" backshifts to "would" and "tomorrow" to "the next day".

options: She said that she could swim.
She said that she can swam.
She told that I could swim.
expl: "Can" normally changes to "could" in reported speech.

options: He said that he had seen him the previous day.
He said that he saw him tomorrow.
He said he sees him yesterday.
He told that he had saw him.
expl: Simple past may backshift to past perfect; "yesterday" becomes "the previous day".

q: The teacher said, "The earth revolves around the sun."
options: The teacher said that the earth revolved around the sun only.
The teacher said that the earth revolves around the sun.
The teacher told that the earth has revolved.
expl: Universal truths usually remain in the present tense.

q: He said to me, "Do you know the answer?"
options: He asked me if I knew the answer.
He told me do I know the answer.
He asked that I know answer.
He said me whether do I knew.
expl: Yes/no questions use asked + if/whether + statement word order.

options: She asked where was I going.
She asked where I was going.
She said where I am going.
She asked that where I went.
expl: Wh-question keeps the question word but uses statement word order.

options: The officer ordered them to stand at ease.
The officer said that stand at ease.
expl: Commands are commonly reported with ordered/told + object + to-infinitive.

options: He requested me to help him.
He said me please to help.
He asked that I helped him yesterday.
expl: Polite requests are reported with requested/asked + object + to-infinitive.

options: Mother advised me not to waste time.
Mother said me do not waste time.
Mother told that not waste time.
expl: Negative commands/advice use not to + verb.

options: He exclaimed with sorrow that he had failed.
He said alas that he fails.
He exclaimed with joy that he had failed.
expl: "Alas" expresses sorrow; present perfect backshifts.

options: She exclaimed with joy that they had won.
She exclaimed with sorrow that they won.
She said hurrah we have won.
She ordered that they had won.
expl: "Hurrah" expresses joy.

options: He prayed that I might succeed.
He said that I may succeeded.
expl: Wishes/prayers are often reported with prayed/wished + might.

q: "This" generally changes to ___ in reported speech when distance shifts.
expl: "This" commonly changes to "that".
"Now" commonly becomes "then" when the reporting perspective shifts.
"Here" commonly becomes "there".

q: Which reporting verb is most suitable for a question?
expl: Questions are generally reported with "asked" or "inquired".
